title: The repository.publish_resolve service: an operator-asserted resolve that records a REFUSED receipt and releases the PUBLISHING hold
description:
CHILD of task-21be6e9055984413a651ce6ee331e2c8 (the operator exit for an UNKNOWN publish), filed by architect-73d103f8 on 2026-09-18. Delivers the daemon half of that row's DoD 2 and DoD 4's release reason. task-21be6e90 is the integration parent and declares dependsOn on this row.

WHAT IT DOES. Replaces the refusing stub that row 3 (task-2c3f878ba94940428d34f204dc74de95) registers for `repository.publish_resolve` with the real behaviour, in a NEW module apps/daemon/src/repository/publish-resolve-service.ts (plus its one-line .js bridge — plain-node entries now load the daemon graph without transform flags, so a missing bridge is a runtime failure, not a style issue). Given `{ decisionId, resolution: \"NOT_TRANSMITTED\" | \"ABANDON\" }` from the operator:
- refuse with row 2's codes (task-adeabf1f8c9e4e2c8b778491f9e20b71) when the decision names no publish request, when it is NOT UNKNOWN (it already has a receipt, or no intent), or, for NOT_TRANSMITTED, when the recorded observation shows the remote DOES hold the approved sha;
- otherwise record a REFUSED receipt for THAT decisionId carrying the last observation, and release the reservation from PUBLISHING with a NEW reason `PUBLISH_RESOLVED`, legal only from PUBLISHING.

WHY A NEW REASON. task-78dea88b adds `PUBLISH_NOT_TRANSMITTED` for a resolve the DAEMON PROVED. This one is ASSERTED BY THE OPERATOR; distinct reasons keep the audit trail honest about who decided. Add it to `RepositoryExecutionReleaseReason` (apps/daemon/src/repository/repository-execution-contracts.ts:10) and one branch to the reason-to-phase ternary at repository-execution-port.ts:101-105, keeping the chain's fall-through to false so an unlisted reason still fails closed.

WHY THE CARD UN-STICKS FOR FREE. apps/daemon/src/http/run-goal-publication.ts skips any decision that already has a receipt BEFORE consulting its intent (`if (state.receipts.has(pending.decisionId)) continue;`), so a REFUSED receipt for the SAME decisionId flips the card from UNKNOWN to REFUSED and re-enables Publish — the same mechanism task-78dea88b relies on.

THE SINGLE-TRANSMISSION INVARIANT. The resolve never pushes. It only records the operator's assertion and releases the hold; a later publish is a FRESH decision with its own intent. The arms in apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/node-publisher-approved.test.ts must pass UNCHANGED.

Depends on row 3 (the registered stub and fence) and task-78dea88b (the transmission evidence and the NOT_TRANSMITTED reason, which edit repository-execution-contracts.ts and -port.ts first).
definitionOfDone: An operator resolve of an UNKNOWN publish records a REFUSED receipt for that decisionId carrying the last observation, and releases the reservation from PUBLISHING with reason PUBLISH_RESOLVED; asserted by value on the receipt, the reservation's absence and the reason, and `readRunGoalPublication` then reports REFUSED rather than UNKNOWN for that decision.

Every refusal is asserted by exact code WITH its layer from row 2's map: an unknown decision id; a decision that is not UNKNOWN (already PUSHED or REFUSED, or with no intent); and NOT_TRANSMITTED against an observation showing the remote holds the approved sha. Each refusing arm asserts the reservation is UNCHANGED.

PUBLISH_RESOLVED is accepted only from PUBLISHING: a repository-execution-port.test.ts arm sweeps the port's own phase list, asserts the sweep visited more than one phase, and asserts the exact refusal from every other phase.
The resolve never transmits: the injected publication port records ZERO push calls across every arm, and node-publisher-approved.test.ts passes unchanged.
Gates quoted with `Test Files N passed` lines: daemon tests for src/repository/** and src/orchestrator/node-publisher*, the full `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, and `pnpm typecheck`.

NEW publish-resolve-service.ts (~75 lines). It imports only store, the ledgers and row 2's contracts. It has NO repository-execution import and takes no port.
`resolvePublish(store, {projectId, decisionId, resolution, decidedAt})`:
- It finds the request by walking readPublishLedger.
- It refuses with row 2's constructor only; no call site passes a layer:
  - PUBLISH_RESOLVE_DECISION_NOT_FOUND when the decision is unknown;
  - PUBLISH_RESOLVE_NOT_UNKNOWN when the decision already has a receipt, or has no intent. An intent that cannot be read counts as UNKNOWN, as it does on the card;
  - PUBLISH_RESOLVE_REMOTE_HOLDS_SHA for NOT_TRANSMITTED when the LATEST observation's observedSha equals the approved sha.
- Otherwise it writes ONE REFUSED receipt through recordPublishReceipt. The code is PUBLISH_RESOLVED_{NOT_TRANSMITTED|ABANDON}. The detail is "the operator resolved this publish as <R>; last observation <at>: remote tip <sha|absent>, expected <sha>, push <reason>", or "...; no observation of the remote was recorded".
- If another writer's receipt lands first, it answers NOT_UNKNOWN.
- If the write itself fails, it throws DurableStoreError (EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT, or STORE_CORRUPT), which the decision port maps to 503 at DURABLE_STORE.
- It exports PUBLISH_RESOLVED_CODES and isPublishResolvedCode for step 4. The PublishResolution type is derived from those codes.

TESTS, 8 arms. Every refusal is asserted with toStrictEqual on {ok, code, layer "DAEMON_PREREQUISITE", detail}, plus "no receipt written" and "hold untouched":
- unknown id;
- PUSHED and REFUSED receipts (sweep count 2; the receipt is left as it was);
- no intent;
- NOT_TRANSMITTED against a latest observation at the approved sha.
The success arms:
- NOT_TRANSMITTED: exactly one receipt and one RepositoryPublishRefused event, with the exact detail taken from the LATEST of two observations. The card goes from UNKNOWN to REFUSED with its code, and `observation: null`. That pins task-52682237's unpinned `receipt === undefined` guard, as its follow-up asked.
- ABANDON with an observation at the approved sha, and with none (sweep count 2).
- The code roster, and isPublishResolvedCode false on 5 foreign codes.
- A Proxy store that fails the commit throws DurableStoreError EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT with the exact message, and records no receipt.

ZERO RESERVATION CALLS: the hold is a REAL PUBLISHING reservation on a temp git repo, owned by "wrapper-controller". Every arm asserts `port.inspect(root)` equals the fixture's reservation exactly (phase, revision, controller). This is a persisted-state proof: any release, claim or transition by any path would change it.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW (step 6C) AND CORRECTIONS (6D). task-a47babf8, worker-952c612b.

(D) CORRECTION TO THE DESCRIPTION. The command CANNOT release the hold. repository-execution-port.ts:100 refuses any controller but the reservation's own with REPOSITORY_EXECUTION_CONTROLLER_MISMATCH, and the new port arm pins that from PUBLISHING. During a stuck publish, the owner is the live wrapper's publisher controller, a random id per process (repository-delivery-runtime.ts:195). So the service records the operator's resolution as ONE REFUSED receipt (PUBLISH_RESOLVED_NOT_TRANSMITTED|ABANDON), and the OWNING publisher releases the hold on its next pass as PUBLISH_RESOLVED. repository.recover uses the same pattern: record a fact, and the owner acts on it.
Also corrected: planningNotes (3). The decision port writes nothing (daemon-command-decision-port.ts:75). Attribution rests on two things: only the configured operator passes the entry fence, and only this service writes PUBLISH_RESOLVED_* codes.

(C1) CAN THE COMMAND REACH THE RESERVATION PORT? No.
- Neither the service nor the command imports a repository-execution module (`grep -n repository-execution` on both is empty), and the service takes no port and no workspace.
- Every service arm asserts that a REAL persisted PUBLISHING reservation (a temp git repo) is unchanged: same phase, revision and controller. That catches a release, claim or transition made by any path.

(C2) TRANSMITS TWICE?
- A resolved decision never reaches `transmit`: the settled branch returns before any push or observe.
- The window arms, for both ledger orders, show the fresh decision pushing EXACTLY once. The restart arm uses a git port that throws on any call.
- HONEST LIMIT, NOT_TRANSMITTED against a push that DID land. The guard refuses only when the LATEST recorded observation is at the approved sha. node-publisher never records that (node-publisher.ts:205-210: it observes only when the tip differs, and equality writes PUSHED), so against today's producer the guard is dormant.
- There is a residual window: a push landed but was never receipted, because the wrapper died between push and receipt, or because the resolve's receipt beat the publisher's PUSHED in a cross-process race. In that window NOT_TRANSMITTED is accepted and D1's audit line is false.
- The next decision's preflight then reads tip == approved sha, and `contains` is true, so its push of the SAME sha is a git no-op. That is a second transmission ATTEMPT but no second effect.
- Follow-up for the epic-final row: refuse NOT_TRANSMITTED when the transmission record says ACCEPTED. That needs a code, and row 2's vocabulary is closed.

(C3) WRAPPER DOWN AT RESOLVE TIME.
- The receipt is durable, and the card reads REFUSED at once.
- Meanwhile the hold stays PUBLISHING: deliveries are REPOSITORY_EXECUTION_BUSY, and a fresh publish WAITs. Nothing is lost.
- On restart, the new controller claims the dead one (processAlive false) and releases PUBLISH_RESOLVED on its first pass. The restart arm proves this with exactly 1 claim and zero remote calls.
- A live foreign controller is never taken over (publicationReservation).

(C4) MISTAKEN FOR A RESOLVE? `settled` requires PUBLISH_NOT_LANDED or EXACT membership in PUBLISH_RESOLVED_CODES. Four foreign codes, including the lookalikes PUBLISH_RESOLVED and PUBLISH_RESOLVE_NOT_UNKNOWN, leave the hold alone (arm 2), and drill S6 reds it. Both writers use the node-publisher principal, so the code is the only discriminator. The service header says no other writer may mint these codes.

OTHER RESIDUALS (none of them block):
- A retry of the same command after success answers NOT_UNKNOWN. That is truthful and writes no second receipt, but the answer is not REPLAYED, because there is no admission journal.
- An unreadable intent counts as UNKNOWN, as on the card, so it is resolvable. But the publisher's release pass reads the intent first, and a corrupt intent keeps the hold (pre-existing).
- There is no project or transport check. The kind is off every MCP roster, the fence requires the configured operator, and the ledger read is scoped to the daemon's project. Row 2's vocabulary has no code for either check.
- A paired-browser human is still refused 403 (comment-ca397fbb on task-21be6e90).
- Receipt-key poisoning under a version race: filed as bug task-978669b6.
- Docs: apps/daemon/CLAUDE.md has no bullet yet on publish_resolve and PUBLISH_RESOLVED. That is left to the epic's docs sweep.

planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Filed by me today as a CHILD of task-21be6e90. dependsOn [task-2c3f878b (row 3's registered stub and fence), task-78dea88b (the transmission evidence and the port's first new release reason), task-52682237 (the observation this service checks and carries)]. That third dependency was MISSING when the chain was first wired and was added while planning this row: without the observation reader, an operator could assert NOT_TRANSMITTED on a push that actually landed, and the next publish would transmit a second time. Measured at HEAD 2026-09-18.

(1) THE DESCRIPTION'S CORE MECHANISM IS UNIMPLEMENTABLE AS WRITTEN — measured. It says the service 'releases the reservation from PUBLISHING with a NEW reason PUBLISH_RESOLVED'. apps/daemon/src/repository/repository-execution-port.ts `release(workspace, owner, expectedRevision, reason, controllerId)` begins `if (controllerId !== prior.state.controllerId) return repositoryExecutionFailure("REPOSITORY_EXECUTION_CONTROLLER_MISMATCH")`. The PUBLISHING reservation is owned by the WRAPPER's publisher controller: apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/node-publisher-reservation.ts takes a handle only when `handle.reservation.controllerId === config.controller.controllerId`, and returns null while another controller's process is ALIVE (it may `claimController` only a dead one). During a stuck publish that wrapper is alive, passing UNKNOWN every tick. A command handler runs in the DAEMON under a different controller, so it can never release that hold.

(2) THE PRECEDENT FOR THIS EXACT SITUATION. `repository.recover`, an operator-only command in REPOSITORY_RECOVERY_FAMILY, manipulates reservations it does not own by RECORDING A FACT that the owning controller then acts on (apps/daemon/src/repository/repository-recovery-facts.ts; read back at repository-landing-attempt.ts via `readRecoveryFact`). Controller ownership is the invariant that stops two processes racing on one reservation; the resolve respects it the same way.

(3) THE RECEIPT IS THE FACT — no new ledger event. The command writes a REFUSED publish receipt for the decision through the existing `recordPublishReceipt` (the call node-publisher already uses), with a resolve code naming the resolution and a detail carrying the last observation. Who asserted it is already durable: every dispatched command is a recorded decision carrying its principal. That keeps publication-effect-ledger.ts untouched and the row at exactly ten files, where a separate 'resolve requested' event would have forced another split.

(4) WHY THE CARD FLIPS IMMEDIATELY. apps/daemon/src/http/run-goal-publication.ts skips any decision that already has a receipt before consulting its intent (`if (state.receipts.has(pending.decisionId)) continue;`), so the card reports REFUSED as soon as the command writes the receipt.

(5) WHY node-publisher MUST ACT, OR THE HOLD IS STRANDED. With a receipt on the decision, the publisher no longer treats it as pending; unless taught otherwise it never releases the PUBLISHING hold it owns, and every later delivery stays REPOSITORY_EXECUTION_BUSY. So node-publisher, on its next pass, must release a PUBLISHING hold it owns whose decision now carries an operator-resolve receipt, with the new reason PUBLISH_RESOLVED.

(6) THE PORT HAS ALREADY MOVED. repository-execution-port.ts's release guard now reads `reason === "PUBLISHED" || reason === "PUBLISH_NOT_TRANSMITTED" ? prior.state.phase === "PUBLISHING"` — task-78dea88b's reason has landed there. PUBLISH_RESOLVED joins that same branch.

(7) ROW 3'S STUB ARM FLIPS. task-2c3f878b pins, in apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.test.ts, that an OPERATOR dispatch of `repository.publish_resolve` is refused by its stub. Replacing the stub makes that arm wrong by design; it must be re-aimed to the real behaviour, not deleted.
